messages:
Anya: Heads-up — after last night's kernel-selector tweak I see sustained memory growth for long sessions when using INT8 runtime. KV page counts slowly increase over ~5-10 minute sessions and we end up paged-out slots + eviction storms.

Sasha: Ugh. Which model/variant and which selector weights? :thinking_face:

Anya: model=redwood/13b-openql-int8-v2, selector weights bumped to prefer kernel_v5 for sparse matmul. Batch heuristics: max_batch_tokens=2048, eager_batch_fill=false. Observed on dedicated infra (g5xl-like nodes).

Jun: Can you paste the small profiler snippet? even a flame or top-allocs helps.

Anya: sure — pasted low-noise snippet below (raw):

```
KV pages: total=864 -> 1120 over 6m
slot_count: 4232 -> 7041
evict_ops/sec: 0.2 -> 4.6
avg_page_size_bytes: 16384 -> 8192
fragmentation_ratio: 0.32 -> 0.62
```

Mike: interesting that avg page size halved. suggests the int8 path changed alignment/packing and we now create more smaller pages which hurts coalescing.

perf-bot: perf/traces/2412345678/snapshot-1 -> https://perf.internal/snap/2412345678

Sasha: do we have the slot layout dump from kv_inspect? that shows chain lengths and free-run proportions.

Mike: i ran kv_inspect quickly on the canary node:

```
$ ./kv_inspect --node canary-12 --json
{
  slabs: [64, 32, 32, 64, 16, 16, 8, 8, ...]
  free_runs: 1.2%
  avg_chain_len: 4.1
}
```

Anya: free_runs so low. Also noticed paging pattern: we repeatedly allocate small pages then evict 2x larger prefix pages later — it's like warmup creates fragmentation that the compactor doesn't catch.

Jun: hypothesis: INT8 kernel changed KV value width and our slot_alignment remained 64 -> misaligned tail slots. compaction expects homogenous sizes so mixing 16/32/64 leads to poor coalescing. try forcing slot_alignment=16 in runtime and simulate.

Elaine: we should also check batching heuristics: smaller batches more often = more distinct KV prefixes -> less reuse and higher churn. could be interacting.

Anya: confirmed in traces: increased small-batch rate after selector tweak. Eager_batch_fill=false means more single-request batches during spikes.

Mike: quick repro plan —
- pin kernel selector to kernel_v4 for canary (rollback weight)
- run kv_inspect periodic dumps
- toggle slot_alignment to 16 on one node
- run long session runner (3k token dialog) x10

Sasha: +1. Also add a metric for avg_kv_reuse_distance and page_alloc_rate.

perf-bot: metric created: runtime.kv.avg_kv_reuse_distance

Anya: ran one trial with slot_alignment=16 and kernel_v4 pinned. results: slot_count stabilized ~4400, fragmentation ratio down to 0.28, evict_ops/sec ~0.4. Accuracy delta vs int8 baseline: -0.8% on mean next-token prob (within alert threshold but worth tracking).

Jun: that suggests alignment change helps memory but accuracy tradeoff small. Maybe we can do a hybrid: align to 32 and keep kernel_v5 but adjust its packing so slots are coalescable.

Mike: kernel vendor note — sparse matmul packer has an option `pack_stride` default 64; lowering to 32 reduces padding. Worth trying.

Anya: quick patch tested: pack_stride=32 + slot_alignment=32 on canary. results: slot_count ~4700, fragmentation 0.35, accuracy delta -0.3%. Eviction storms gone.

Elaine: sounds promising. plan: A/B 10% traffic with these settings for 24h, monitor token cost and accuracy regressions and rollback if mean-next-token drops >1.5% or latency increases.

Sasha: I'll update rollout config: route.policy=canary, canary_pct=0.10, monitor=[runtime.kv.fragmentation, model.accuracy.mntp, latency.p95]

Anya: I'll open a short PR with the runtime knobs + test harness changes. cc @Jun @Mike for review.

Jun: I'll run a sim to ensure compactor picks up mixed-size pages within 60s windows.

Mike: also add a small sampling hook that captures a kv page map with token offsets every 30s — adds 0.5% overhead but helps root cause if it returns.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary rollout at 02:00 UTC (canary-ids: canary-12, canary-17)

Anya: thanks — i'll post the PR link and attach the longer traces once available. :thumbsup:

Sasha: thx team — keep logs concise in the PR, but great detective work.
